stages.heading: Wherever you're starting
stages.intro: Most job advice assumes you're already halfway there. {brand} starts from where you actually are.

cards.title: Starting from zero
cards.body: No experience, no network, no idea where to begin. {brand} picks your first three moves: one event, one skill to show off, and one person worth meeting.

cards.title: Skills, but no callbacks
cards.body: You've applied everywhere and heard nothing. {brand} shifts your time from applications to the conversations that get your name in front of people who hire.

cards.title: Interviews coming up
cards.body: You're getting calls. {brand} helps you prepare for that exact role, practise out loud, and follow up so you're the one they remember.

actions.heading: The actions most people skip
actions.intro: Job boards show you postings. {brand} shows you what to do about them, one small step at a time.
actions.featureBody: Tell {brand} the role you want. Each week it checks local events, company news and new job postings, then gives you three things to do, with the words already drafted. You do the actions; {brand} does the homework.

cards.title: Event radar
cards.body: Pulls meetups, hackathons and career fairs near you that match your target role, and flags which companies will be in the room.

cards.title: What to say
cards.body: A short, natural opener for the people you'll meet, based on who they are and what they're working on. No scripts that sound like scripts.

cards.title: Things to talk about
cards.body: Two or three real topics per company, from their recent news, product launches and the tech they hire for, so the conversation goes past "so, what do you do?"

cards.title: Funding watch
cards.body: Startups that just raised money are about to hire. {brand} watches funding news, including new Y Combinator batches and local raises, and tells you when to reach out.

cards.title: Follow-up nudges
cards.body: Met someone? {brand} reminds you within 24 hours and drafts the message. You always review it and hit send yourself.

cards.title: Interview practice
cards.body: Practise out loud for the specific role, with questions built from the actual posting. Get feedback on what to tighten.

week.heading: What a week with {brand} looks like
week.intro: Small, specific moves, each one built on the last.
week.introMuted: These are example actions, not real users.
week.label: Example plan

cards.title: Monday · Funding news
cards.body: A Calgary software startup just announced a new funding round. Send its engineering lead three lines: congrats, one thing you liked about the product, and a question.

cards.title: Tuesday · Pick your event
cards.body: Two meetups this week. {brand} recommends Thursday's: the speaker's company posted a junior role, and smaller rooms mean real conversations.

cards.title: Wednesday · Prep the room
cards.body: Five talking points for Thursday, one per company likely to attend, each tied to something they shipped or announced recently.

cards.title: Thursday · Show up
cards.body: Your opener for the speaker, plus one question that shows you actually read their work. Ten minutes of prep, not two hours.

cards.title: Friday · Follow up
cards.body: You met three people. {brand} drafted three short follow-ups from your notes. Edit, send, and log who replied.

cards.title: Weekend · Practise
cards.body: One of them mentioned an opening. Do a 10-minute practice interview for that exact role before Monday.

items.q: Do I still need to apply to jobs?
items.a: Yes. {brand} doesn't replace applying; it adds the actions that make applications work. Most people only apply and wait. {brand} adds the events, conversations and follow-ups that get your name in front of the person who decides.

items.q: How is this different from asking ChatGPT?
items.a: A chatbot gives advice when you ask. {brand} checks real local events, company news and funding announcements every week, remembers what you've already done, and hands you the next three actions without you having to ask the right question.

items.q: Where do the events and news come from?
items.a: Public sources: event listings, job postings, company announcements and startup funding news. Each action shows where its information came from, so you can check it yourself.
No. {brand} drafts openers and follow-ups, but you always review, edit and send them yourself. Nothing goes out in your name without you.

items.q: What do you store about me?
items.a: Your goals and notes stay on your device by default. Sharing anonymous outcomes, like which events led to interviews, is opt-in, and you can delete everything at any time.

items.q: Is it only for tech jobs?
items.a: We're starting with tech roles, because event and funding data is easiest to find for them. The same approach (show up, talk, follow up) works in any field, and more are on the roadmap.

items.q: Which cities does it work in?
items.a: Calgary first. {brand} is built at a Calgary hackathon and tuned to local events and companies. Other cities come next.
